appliesTo: news-claim-check@1 -- the three `admit` questions, checked against a claim and its cited excerpts. Cases are CONSTRUCTED, so every label is true BY CONSTRUCTION rather than sampled from a real article: the relation is decided by the wording of the excerpt, not by a fact anyone had to look up. Six cases because the battery floor is five and the six are the six ways the production relation goes -- exact support, contradicted figure, no evidence, adjacent subject, right subject with the figure missing, and the figure right but the date wrong.

cases.note: The excerpt states the figure, the year and the subject in so many words. `supported`, `true`, `directly` are entailed.
cases.state:
CLAIM: The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy.

CITED EXCERPTS:
- https://example.org/survey-results-2024: "The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy, the results published on 3 March."

expected.admit_evidence_directness: directly: an excerpt that states the claim's figure or date in so many words

cases.note: Same survey, same year, same subject, and the figure is different. The relation is `contradicted`, and the excerpt is still about the exact claim, so `true` and `directly` hold.
cases.state:
CLAIM: The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy.

CITED EXCERPTS:
- https://example.org/survey-results-2024: "The 2024 national survey found that 41% of adults support the proposed policy, the results published on 3 March."

expected.admit_evidence_directness: directly: an excerpt that states the claim's figure or date in so many words

cases.note: Nothing was retrieved. The relation cannot be decided, and there is no evidence to be direct or partial about.
cases.state:
CLAIM: The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy.

CITED EXCERPTS: (none -- retrieval returned nothing)

expected.admit_evidence_directness: not at all: there is no excerpt, or the excerpt is about a different subject

cases.note: A real excerpt from a real page, about transport rather than the survey. It cannot bear on the claim, so the relation is undecidable rather than supported.
cases.state:
CLAIM: The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy.

CITED EXCERPTS:
- https://example.org/council-minutes: "The city council approved a new bus route on the north side; operators report ridership up 9% since March."

expected.admit_evidence_directness: not at all: there is no excerpt, or the excerpt is about a different subject

cases.note: The excerpt is about the right survey and never states the figure. It is on-topic (`true`) but only partly direct, and it cannot settle the relation.
cases.state:
CLAIM: The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy.

CITED EXCERPTS:
- https://example.org/survey-methodology: "The national survey is carried out by the national statistics office between May and June each year, using a representative sample of 12,000 households."

expected.admit_evidence_directness: partly: an excerpt on the right subject that never states the claim's figure or date

cases.note: The figure is exactly right and the year is wrong. The question says the relation covers dates, so this is `contradicted` -- the case that separates a set which reads the number from one that reads the claim.
cases.state:
CLAIM: The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy.

CITED EXCERPTS:
- https://example.org/archive-2023: "The 2023 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy, the results published on 4 April."

expected.admit_evidence_directness: directly: an excerpt that states the claim's figure or date in so many words
